parole.significato: One of a number of alternative forms of the same gene occupying a given position, or locus, on a chromosome.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Allel, shortened from Allelomorph, from English allelomorph. Ultimately from the Ancient Greek ἀλλήλων (allḗlōn, “each other”) from ἄλλος (állos, “other”).

parole.significato: Military forces considered to be expendable.
parole.testo: Mid-19th century, from cannon (“artillery piece”) + fodder (“food”), a calque of German Kanonenfutter, itself possibly a calque of English food for powder. See the German for more.

parole.significato: A musical style of the 18th century, featuring "true" feelings and sudden mood changes.
parole.testo: From German Empfindsamkeit (“sensibility, sentimentality”). The German term might derive from English sensibility, a related English literature movement from the same time period.
From German Fußball, itself a calque of English football.

parole.significato: A naturally occurring pentose sugar, which is a component of the nucleosides and nucleotides that constitute the nuclei…
parole.testo: From German Ribose, formed from Ribonsäure, the first element of which comes from a rearrangement of English arabinose.
